_about: Semantic gold for the retrieval POC (identity, memberships, forbidden relations), labelled by Claude as a hedge-fund analyst on 2026-10-25 at Alex's request ('金标你来定'). Each label names the ledger (G grouped English poc-v21 english-groups4; E ungrouped English poc-v17/18 english-2026-10-25; C Chinese T4c; S sealed Chinese) and exact view ids. 'same' = one quantity or event under two wordings (a merge was right); 'related' = one matter, different quantity (one group, two theses); 'different' = neither. Labels are an analyst's reading of the stored questions and their initiating evidence, not the model's agreement; disagreements are listed under 'uncertain'.

same.why: both track NVIDIA FY2027 standalone CPU (Vera) revenue; v16's evidence says the ~$20bn forecast is for standalone CPUs
the reported ~$250bn guarantee for OpenAI's data-center lease and debt financing under three wordings (guarantee, financial backstop, financing)

v21's source sentence after the stored quote: 'Nvidia is separately discussing financing the accelerators going inside, which could run to another $350 billion' = v18's chip financing; the extraction attached the preceding guarantee sentence as the quote (restored to same, 2026-10-25)

related_not_same.why: AI infrastructure spending vs accelerator TAM: spending vs market size
guarantee of lease/debt financing vs financing of chip purchases: two arrangements of one deal
chip financing vs the project's total cost including chips
2026 vs 2027 hyperscaler capex: succession, never a merge
non-GAAP vs GAAP tax rate: two bases even with equal guidance
Microsoft capex level 2026 vs FY2027 capex growth
AMD data-center revenue level vs growth
AMD FY2026 vs FY2027 total revenue: succession

the Japan-funded power plant supplies 'the electricity for the facility', the Ohio campus whose financing v17 guarantees: one project, two financings (relabelled from different, 2026-10-25, after Codex's blind review)
SpaceX's capex is tied by its source to the same AI-investment cycle as hyperscaler capex; not a subset, not unrelated (relabelled from different)

top-five cloud providers' capex 2026 vs tech giants' AI-infrastructure spending 2026: the stored questions name different populations and scopes; the sources cite a similar ~$700bn figure, which does not establish one quantity (scored as related; population uncertainty recorded)
hyperscaler capex (its source says 'by 2027') vs AI-infrastructure spending 'this year': different scopes and periods
same pair as G v1/v20 in the Chinese ledger

part_of.why: standalone CPU revenue is a part of total revenue; never a merge, never a dependency by itself
Amazon North America segment revenue is a part of total revenue

identity._labels: same = one quantity or event under two wordings (a merge was right); part_of = the first is a strict component or subset of the second (two theses, no merge); related_not_same = one matter, different quantities (one group, two theses); different = neither. Codex's review (2026-10-25) found the two part-of pairs filed under different; they are now their own class so a classifier's part_of answer scores against them.
identity._visibility: E v61 (Indosat) was created at sequence 318, after the frozen E cutoff 311 used in the census; it is held out of any scoring on that snapshot and scored only on a later completed one.

rubin_rollout.matter: Blackwell/Vera Rubin production rollout and its customer deployments
rubin_rollout.why: shipments, the Blackwell+Rubin revenue opportunity, the Vera CPU figure and the Rubin-based factories (SK Telecom, NAVER, Indosat) are one rollout; PC/RTX products, developer tools and NVIDIA's company lines are not Standalone Vera CPU revenue (G v13, E v12, C v11) is optional, not required: the same transcript calls it 'a brand new $200 billion TAM' and Huang excludes standalone CPU from the Rubin/Blackwell revenue figure (relabelled 2026-10-25 after a second reading; Jev's answers were known at the time and are not the reason). E v18 (the NVIDIA-SK initiative's $500bn business value) is optional: the partnership's first factory deploys Vera Rubin, but the figure is a deal value, not the rollout.

hyperscaler_capex_cycle.matter: the hyperscalers' AI capital-spending cycle: aggregates and each company's own capex
hyperscaler_capex_cycle.why: an analyst following the capex cycle wants every hyperscaler's capex thesis and the aggregates in one place (so Amazon and Alphabet in, Meta and Microsoft in too: the inconsistency F7 is a miss); revenue, margins, segments and Reality Labs losses are not the capex cycle E v35 (Microsoft FY2027 capex growth) is required: 'we expect FY27 capital expenditures will grow year-over-year' tracks the cycle directly.

openai_nvidia_financing.matter: the OpenAI–NVIDIA financing arrangements and the Ohio campus
openai_nvidia_financing.why: guarantee, chip financing, project cost and aggregate transactions are one deal; Japan's power plant and the hyperscaler capex aggregates are not C v19 (Japan's $33bn gas plant) is required: its source says the plant supplies 'the electricity for the facility', the Ohio campus (relabelled from forbidden, 2026-10-25: Jev's 0.68 was right and the first gold wrong).
openai_nvidia_financing.note: no English ledger holds a thesis for this matter (finding F2); the group cannot be scored there

china_chip_export_controls.matter: US and allied export-control actions on AI chips to China and NVIDIA's China access
china_chip_export_controls.why: H200 authorisation, the revenue-share rate, Taiwan's controls and ban, the Remote Access Security Act are one policy process; the sugar tariff-rate quota is not C labels (v8 H200 licence, v9 AI Diffusion replacement rule, v25 Taiwan controls required; v14 US restrictions on Chinese AI models optional: the quote speaks of restricting access to US chips, the thesis of restrictions on the models) were added on 2026-10-25 after the three-state run, from the theses' texts and quotes.

separate_company_matters.why: each is its own matter; a group of one is acceptable; none may join the Rubin or capex groups

_disputes.why: 'capital expenditure on AI alone' vs 'AI hyperscaler capital expenditures': the second never says it covers all uses, so neither same nor a strict part is established; not scored

uncertain.why: Sovereign AI business revenue: a product/region figure; could belong to a sovereign-AI matter if one existed; no label
NVIDIA share of the accelerator market: related to the TAM thesis v20; measure 'growth_rate' is a misfit; no label
Xbox return to growth as a yes/no on a growth_rate measure; a company line; no group

_labels_added_after_runs: C labels for rubin_rollout, hyperscaler_capex_cycle and china_chip_export_controls were added on 2026-10-25 after the three-state POC had run (log row 33); scores on C are therefore completed post hoc and are reported as such.

_notes.forbidden_lists: company reporting lines (total and segment revenue, margins, tax, opex, Reality Labs' operating loss) are measures in FINANCIAL_LINES; D165 lets them join a group another thesis founded, and they stay forbidden members of the Rubin, capex (revenue lines) and China matters by meaning: a line's absence from a group is right, its presence wrong.
_notes.capex_lines: each hyperscaler's own capex thesis is a required member of the capex cycle. D165 permits it ('the lines may join a group another thesis founded'); the only thing that kept them out was the engine asking membership for matter-tracking candidates alone. Counted as misses, not set aside (2026-10-25, after Codex's review).
_notes.helios: E v56 (Helios shipments) and v57 (Anthropic's MI450 deployment 'in Helios') are one AMD matter; no card exists for it, so no membership is scored.
